clue.text: Gus is at Rita's new house

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of the preceding words are made into something fresh, a rearrangement

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter, leaving the name Rita

explanation.surface: Gus is visiting Rita's newly bought home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new house' looks like a property, but 'house' is an astrological house of the zodiac, and 'new' rearranges GUS IS AT RITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrologers call each of the twelve zodiac signs a house, and the Archer is one of them.

clue.text: Posed for nearly half a day

indicators.note: nearly means the piece falls just short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: the first half of the word Saturday, a day of the week, is SATU

explanation.surface: Someone modelled for an artist for close to twelve hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half a day' is not twelve hours but half the letters of SATURDAY; 'nearly' then cuts the U.
explanation.definitionFit: A model who posed for a portrait sat for the artist; the past tenses match.

clue.text: Individual captured by Greek, one with no future

indicators.note: captured by means the first piece is held inside the second

parts.note: an individual is one, a single thing

explanation.surface: A lone man taken prisoner by a Greek soldier is doomed.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone doomed or past saving, with no future ahead of them.

clue.text: Office worker set out to produce violent agitation

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of the next word are put out of order

explanation.surface: A temp in the office deliberately stirs up trouble among colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal, applied to the short word after it; 'set' is not a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, and by extension any violent commotion or agitation.

clue.text: Heedful Argentinian politician climbing without portable shelter

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first piece goes round the second
in a down clue, climbing means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: Eva Peron, known as Evita, was an Argentinian political figure
a tent is a shelter that can be carried and pitched anywhere

explanation.surface: A careful Argentinian politician goes climbing without a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses the politician, since a down answer is read upwards; 'without' is the old sense of outside, so the turned name wraps the shelter. Evita is Eva Peron.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedful and attentive are synonyms, both meaning paying close attention.

clue.text: Time to abandon cells? That's the topic for discussion

indicators.note: to abandon means the named letter leaves the word

parts.note: tissue is a mass of cells in a body

explanation.surface: A prisoner asks when it is time to leave the cells, a matter worth debating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cells' suggests a prison, but it is body tissue; removing T leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a matter or subject that people debate.

clue.text: Break beginning to satisfy tea party host

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the Mad Hatter hosts the tea party in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A guest breaks something as they start to please the host of a tea party.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter something is to break it into many pieces.

clue.text: Turkish commander leaves son out of story

indicators.note: leaves means the son is left off the word for story that follows

parts.note: taken from a saga, a long story; out of names where the letter is removed from

explanation.surface: A Turkish officer is written out of a tale, leaving his son behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' and 'out of' work together: the son is dropped from the saga.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga was a military commander or official in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Fairly slow worker at home in a new party

indicators.note: in places the worker and home pieces inside the party

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
an ant is the crossword's standard worker
in means at home

explanation.surface: An employee who is at home attends a fresh party, taking it slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' governs only worker and home, which sit inside the party; the A and the new abbreviation stand in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a musical tempo marking meaning a little faster than andante, a moderately slow pace.

clue.text: Drink producing trouble after morning at checkout?

indicators.note: after places the trouble piece behind the morning and checkout pieces

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem
on can mean at, as in on the till
the till is the cash register at a checkout
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A shopper reaches for a drink after a troublesome morning working the checkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' moves the trouble to the end even though it is printed first; 'at checkout' gives two pieces, the at and the till.
explanation.definitionFit: Amontillado is a medium-dry variety of sherry, a drink.

clue.text: Can Dodie ultimately engross metalworkers?

parts.note: a tin is a can
Dodie Smith was the author of The Hundred and One Dalmatians

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Could the writer Dodie hold the attention of craftsmen in metal?
explanation.walkthrough: Dodie Smith was an English novelist and playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsmiths are craftsmen who work with tin and other light metals.

clue.text: Sound girl wearing a posh ring

indicators.note: wearing means the girl is clothed by the letters from a, posh and ring

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
O looks like a ring
Di is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl wears a ring that looks rather upmarket.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio means relating to sound, as in audio equipment.

clue.text: Naval medic's boy eating egg

indicators.note: eating means the boy piece takes the egg piece inside itself

parts.note: a son is a boy
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: A naval doctor's son tucks into an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg' is not breakfast but the verb, as in egg on, meaning urge.
explanation.definitionFit: Navy medical officers hold the title of surgeon, as in Surgeon Commander.

clue.text: It conceals 9's concern about donkey on slippery slope

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the rest

parts.note: the answer to 9 across deal with tin, whose chemical symbol is Sn

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the donkey piece above the slope piece

parts.note: moke is a British slang word for a donkey
scree is loose stones on a mountain slope

explanation.surface: Metalworkers worry about a donkey slithering down a stony hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sends the chemical symbol round the rest; '9' refers to the metalworkers of 9 across, whose metal's symbol is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A smokescreen hides something, literally with smoke or figuratively with distraction.

clue.text: Wiped out former partner taking money to court

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
tin is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone is ruined by an ex who takes them to court for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A species wiped out has died out completely, which is to say it no longer exists.

clue.text: Attack directions given in Holy Writ

indicators.note: given in means the directions are placed within the scripture

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, part of the Bible
N, S and E are compass directions

explanation.surface: Instructions for an assault are found in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault or attack, as well as a beginning.

clue.text: Cross-eyed person with several siblings involved in scam

indicators.note: involved in means the person is placed inside the scam

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick
a quin is one of quintuplets, so has four siblings born together

explanation.surface: A cross-eyed member of a large family gets drawn into a con.
explanation.definitionFit: Squinting describes eyes that look in different directions, as a cross-eyed person's do.

clue.text: Communicate to single man not taking sides

parts.note: to impart is to pass on or communicate
I is the Roman numeral one
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: A message is passed to a bachelor who refuses to choose sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Impartial means neutral, favouring neither party.

clue.text: Literary production makes us stew

definitions.meaning: a miscellany or medley of literary pieces
the French ... was a stew of mixed meats

explanation.surface: A book so bad that it makes its readers fume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes us' only links the two senses; 'stew' looks like a verb meaning fret but is the old dish of mixed meats.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a medley, whether of writings, of scented petals or, originally, of meats in a stew.

clue.text: In film, Sally given soldiers' kit

indicators.note: In means the joke and soldiers are placed inside the film

parts.note: ET is the famous Spielberg film
a sally is a witty remark, a quip
men are soldiers, the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: In a movie, a girl called Sally is handed military gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a girl's name but is a witty remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment and kit both mean the gear needed for a task.

clue.text: Synthetic device used by shoemaker in film

indicators.note: in places the shoemaker's tool inside the film

parts.note: a pic is an informal word for a film
a last is the foot-shaped block a cobbler works on

explanation.surface: A cobbler's fake tool appears in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic materials are synthetic, man-made rather than natural.

clue.text: For example, Miss Macdonald's list of plants

definitions.meaning: ... Macdonald, the Scottish heroine who helped Bonnie Prince Charlie escape
a catalogue of the plants of a region

explanation.surface: Miss Macdonald has drawn up a catalogue of plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Flora Macdonald helped Bonnie Prince Charlie escape after the 1745 Jacobite rising.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the Scottish heroine and the plant life, or a list of it, of an area.

clue.text: Fine old city relatively great in extent and distance

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
long means great in extent compared with something else

explanation.surface: An ancient city is described as fine and extensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A furlong is a unit of distance, an eighth of a mile, used in horse racing.

clue.text: Record rubbish, a musical composition

parts.note: to can is to record, as in a film in the can
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: A critic calls a recorded piece of music trash.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a vocal composition with soloists, chorus and instruments.

clue.text: Large dish of tea she took

indicators.note: of signals the answer is made from the run of letters within the words

explanation.surface: Someone helped herself to a big plate at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: ASHET is a Scottish and northern English word for a large serving plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashet is a large oval serving dish, a word used in Scotland.

clue.text: Initially old trades were sufficient for an Italian port

indicators.note: Initially takes the opening letters of the next two words

parts.note: if supplies ran to something, they were enough to cover it

explanation.surface: In the past, commerce was enough to sustain an Italian harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Otranto is a port town in the heel of Italy, in Apulia.

clue.text: Aquatic larva reported near boundaries of airfield

indicators.note: reported means a word is given by how it is said

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: boundaries of picks the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A grub is said to have been spotted close to the edges of an airstrip.
explanation.walkthrough: NIGH said aloud gives the opening sound, and AD is the first and last letters of airfield.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is the aquatic larva of insects such as dragonflies and mayflies.

clue.text: One of two writers having thin material rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the word is turned back on itself

parts.note: toile is a thin linen or cotton fabric

explanation.surface: An author turns down some flimsy cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: T S Eliot and George Eliot are the two writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both George Eliot and T S Eliot wrote under this surname.

clue.text: It's blown with great force, mostly by a woman

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is cut

parts.note: hard means with great force
Monica is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman puffs with all her might.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth organ is a wind instrument that is played by being blown into.

clue.text: US jazz instrument unknown in a European capital

indicators.note: in places the unknown inside the other letters
capital means the capital, or first, letter of the next word

parts.note: X is the classic algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An American jazz instrument goes missing in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city but means the capital letter of European.
explanation.definitionFit: In American jazz slang an axe is any instrument, especially a saxophone or guitar.

clue.text: Small horse or badger

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a small or worn-out horse and to pester someone persistently.

clue.text: Leading position 26 requires

definitions.meaning: the forefront, the most advanced position
the answer to 26 down, an axe, needs a sharp blade

explanation.surface: The front line is what an axe needs.
explanation.definitionFit: The forefront of a field is its front line, and an axe needs a sharp blade.
